name: Provider Hub
description: Provider-neutral connection metadata and bounded live-data reads, with the read transport and the digest SHIPPED rather than specified. Production reads are permitted under a named, time-bounded, origin-scoped authorisation. The buyer supplies provider credentials, persistence, authorization policy and deployment.
_minModules: The Provider Hub buyer graph starts at the bounded core index and must include its read adapter, evidence module, acceptance harness and the shipped https transport. A shorter graph means the portable boundary is incomplete or the transport stopped being reachable, which would return the product to the state where a buyer had to write the HTTP client themselves.
_hostFallbacks: Bare or aliased specifiers reached by the buyer graph but supplied by the buyer. Keep empty unless the release gate reports a concrete dependency.
buyerMustSupply: Provider credentials and network policy — the transport is shipped; the account is the buyer’s.
ProviderLiveDataReadTransport — OPTIONAL NOW. createHttpsReadTransport() ships working; supply your own only if you need a protocol it does not cover.
ProviderLiveDataDigestPort — OPTIONAL NOW. createSha256DigestPort() uses the runtime’s own SHA-256.
ProviderConnectionPersistencePort — reads connection metadata from the buyer’s own persistence layer.
A production authorisation record — named approver, approval and expiry timestamps, and the exact https origins it covers. Production reads are refused without one.
Authorization, approval, quota, spend, audit and deployment controls — the payload does not supply production policy or infrastructure.
notIncluded: Provider mutation or write execution. Reads only, in every mode.
Automatic approval, rollout, deployment, or production publication.
A hosted database, vault, network transport, or provider account.
supportedPlatforms: Buyer-selected persistence, vault, and network implementations
Linux and macOS build hosts; no native modules

upgradeCompatibility.policy: Within 1.x the buyer-facing interfaces are additive only.
upgradeCompatibility.ledgerSchema: The payload owns no datastore schema.
upgradeCompatibility.rollback: The payload holds no state and can be replaced by restoring the previous verified archive.

knownLimitations: The release candidate validates packaging and integrity only; it is not evidence of buyer deployment acceptance.
Reads only. There is no write path in the payload, in any execution mode.

The shipped transport speaks HTTPS with bearer, header or basic authentication. A provider requiring request signing (AWS SigV4, OAuth 1.0a) needs a buyer-supplied transport, because a signing implementation we could not verify against their account would be worse than an honest gap.
Production reads require an authorisation record and are refused without one — deliberate, and the reason the gate exists rather than a switch.

acceptance.how: Import the entry point in a clean buyer environment and call runProviderHubAcceptance({ transport, digest, probeUrl }) with the buyer's own transport and digest ports and an https URL the buyer controls. Twelve checks are reported independently; the harness refuses to run without a probe URL rather than substituting a destination of its own.
acceptance.guarantee: The payload contains no credentials and performs no provider mutation, deployment, or automatic production action. Production-mode reads are refused by the adapter and asserted by the first check.
acceptance.evidence: The returned provider-hub-acceptance/1 record is the acceptance artifact. Retain it; it names which properties held and against which probe origin.
